reading: The first refusal of each probe. A refusal masks every later one, so each probe after the first removes what the one before it was refused for, and the map is the first refusal per operation with the earlier ones removed. The probes run in order: the notebook's call as it is; its tables named as the source names them; then without the relationships, the keys and the time columns passed in; then with the columns dropped from the data whose inference the core refuses, one rule at a time, until describe_source succeeds; then the notebook's schema made by editing what the core described (keys, relationships, the products' time column cleared, rowguid deleted) and materialized with inference_config, without it, with one hop, and without the text column, which reaches predict's result on both runners. What the probes removed is the scope this map gives T1.23 to T1.28; a rule no probe reached past (predict with inference_config, a time column cleared in Schema.from_source) is not in it and stays refused (P1B). rust-host starts the core operations, so it has a probe only where the contract can carry the input (gaps).

gaps.input: tables named by another name than their source's ({'customers': 'adventureworks_customers'})
gaps.contract: SourceSpec.tables holds source names only, and DescribedTable a name only, so the core cannot say which source table a schema table reads
SourceSpec has no relationships; the description's links are the declared ones
neither materialize's nor predict's input carries inference options

entries.rule: no_core_route: schema.from-source/tables/duckdb, the path of a call naming its tables, has none in this build
entries.why: T1.24 routes Schema.from_source with tables named onto the core, once T1.23's describe_source takes them (describe_source/tables_named)

entries.rule: no_core_route: a schema Schema.from_source did not describe on the core
entries.why: Reached only by forcing materialize without Schema.from_source; the journey's schema is described on the core once T1.24 routes Schema.from_source with tables named

describe_source's overrides, applied between inference and the key count as the reference applies them; the notebook names each table by another name than its source's, which SourceSpec.tables (source names only) cannot carry, so T1.23 adds the name each table is given

entries.operation: describe_source (refused by the schema bridge before the core runs)
entries.why: The ledger's option refusals pass through to the core (T1.24), which takes the links given once T1.23's describe_source checks and keeps them; SourceSpec has no place for them yet
Text whose values could be dates (seven AdventureWorks columns of codes with digits, such as AccountNumber), which reading dates (DT-7, text_shapes) decides
A timestamp named as an edit stamp (ModifiedDate, in every table), which the time-column choice and the edit stamps the ledger gives T1.23 decide
A timestamp held in fewer than half the rows (products' SellEndDate and DiscontinuedDate)
Several timestamps in one table (the order headers' OrderDate, DueDate and ShipDate)

entries.operation: materialize (refused by the materialize bridge before the core runs)
entries.why: The inference options the call carries (E45(a): only those kumo-relational reads) are written by sdm-request (T1.28); the contract's materialize and predict inputs have no place for them yet, and T1.24 passes the option through to the core rather than refuse it in the bridge
The order lines refer to customers as well as products, so the sample walks past the first hop
A text feature in a sampled table (products' Name), which the reference's sampler normalizes (rfm/base/sampler.py:329-331)

the relationships passed in (the contract has no place for them, so rust-host has no probe of its own)
the time columns given; from here Schema.from_source takes no arguments
the text columns whose values could be dates (text_time)
the four ModifiedDate columns, edit stamps by name (time_name)
products' SellEndDate and DiscontinuedDate, held in fewer than half the rows (time_values)
the order headers' DueDate and ShipDate, beside OrderDate (time_several)

nothing more: the notebook's keys, relationships, cleared time column and deleted columns set by editing the schema the core described, then materialize with inference_config (which the contract has no place for, so rust-host has no probe of its own)
the order lines' link to customers, so the lines refer only to products
